memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the people bowed down and worshiped. The Israelites did just what the LORD
commanded Moses and Aaron." - Ex 12:27b-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two responses, and they belong together: they worshipped, and they obeyed.

Think about how remarkable this is. This is the same people who had complained
bitterly to Moses back in chapter 5, saying he had made their situation worse.
They had refused to listen "because of their discouragement and harsh labor"
(Ex 6:9). Now, after nine plagues and a strange set of instructions about lambs
and doorframes, they bow down and do exactly what God said.

Notice the order. Worship came first, then obedience. That order is important.
Obedience that does not flow from worship becomes duty, and duty eventually
becomes resentment. But when we have seen who God is, obedience follows more
naturally.

Notice also that they obeyed before they saw any result. The blood went on the
doorframes in daylight. The judgment came at midnight. There were hours in
between with nothing to do but wait and trust.

That is where most of us live. We obey in the afternoon and wait for midnight.
Hebrews 11:28 lists this very act among the great works of faith: "By faith he
kept the Passover and the application of blood."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your obedience flowing from worship or from mere duty?
2. What has God asked of you that you are delaying because you cannot see the
   result?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, let my obedience grow out of worship, not obligation. Help me to do what
You have said even when I cannot yet see the outcome. Amen.
